history.hpi: Patient reports sudden onset of palpitations and lightheadedness approximately 10 minutes ago while working. Describes his heart as 'racing' and feels like he might pass out when standing. Denies chest pain, denies any prior episodes like this.
history.lastOralIntake: Multiple energy drinks and coffee throughout the shift, last approximately 30 minutes prior to onset
history.events: Coworker called 911 after the patient became pale, diaphoretic, and reported his heart racing; patient has remained seated to avoid syncope

scene.dispatch: 45-year-old male, chest discomfort and dizziness, workplace
scene.safety: No hazards to crew noted; coworkers present and cooperative
scene.bystanders: Coworker reports patient suddenly became pale and complained of his heart racing after drinking several energy drinks during his shift; coworker called 911 immediately
visualCues: Patient seated, gripping the edge of a table
Several empty energy drink cans on the table nearby

phases.name: Initial Contact
phases.description: Crew arrives to find a 45-year-old male seated, pale and diaphoretic, reporting sudden-onset palpitations and near-syncope. Radial pulse is rapid and weak.

clinicalPresentation.circulation: Radial pulse rapid and weak, regular; skin pale, cool, diaphoretic
otherFindings: Heart rate too fast to count manually, palpated as regular
Reports feeling like he might pass out when standing
No chest pain, no prior cardiac history
clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: "My heart is racing so fast, I feel like I'm going to pass out."

expectedActions.shortAction: Establish O2, cardiac monitor, 12-lead EKG, and IV access
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Manage airway as necessary. Administer oxygen as appropriate with a target of achieving 94–98% saturation. Initiate monitoring and perform 12-lead EKG. Establish IV access.
expectedActions.rationale: Confirms the rhythm on 12-lead and establishes access needed for sedation prior to cardioversion.

expectedActions.shortAction: Check blood glucose to rule out hypoglycemia as a contributing cause
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Check blood glucose and treat hypoglycemia per the Hypoglycemia Guideline
expectedActions.rationale: Hypoglycemia is a listed reversible cause of tachycardia that must be excluded.

expectedActions.shortAction: Recognize hypotension and near-syncope as unstable SVT; bypass the stable pharmacologic pathway
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Regular Narrow Complex Tachycardia – Unstable: Deliver a synchronized shock based on manufacturer's recommendations.
expectedActions.rationale: Vagal maneuvers and adenosine belong to the stable pathway; using them here delays definitive treatment for an unstable patient.

transitions.condition: Crew completes the initial assessment (oxygen, monitor, 12-lead, IV access, blood glucose) and identifies hemodynamic instability (hypotension, near-syncope) meeting criteria for the unstable SVT pathway.
Crew instead attempts vagal maneuvers and/or adenosine as though the patient were hemodynamically stable, delaying definitive synchronized cardioversion.

phases.name: Unstable pathway recognized
phases.description: Crew establishes monitoring, IV access, and checks blood glucose while recognizing that the patient's hypotension and near-syncope place him in the unstable regular narrow complex tachycardia pathway, which calls for synchronized cardioversion rather than stable pharmacologic therapy.
phases.triggerCondition: After completing the initial assessment steps common to all tachycardia patients (oxygen, monitoring, 12-lead, IV access, blood glucose check), the crew recognizes the patient's hypotension (82/54) and near-syncope as signs of hemodynamic instability, meeting protocol criteria for the unstable SVT pathway.

clinicalPresentation.circulation: Radial pulse rapid, weak, regular; skin pale, cool, diaphoretic
otherFindings: IV established, blood glucose 98 mg/dL, ruling out hypoglycemia
Continues to report lightheadedness when upright
clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: "It's not slowing down, I still feel dizzy."

expectedActions.shortAction: Ketamine 22 mg IV for procedural sedation (88 kg × 0.25 mg/kg = 22 mg; max initial 25 mg)
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Ketamine: 0.25 mg/kg IM, IV or IO (maximum initial dose 25 mg; maximum cumulative dose 100 mg)
expectedActions.rationale: Provides sedation and analgesia for a responsive patient prior to cardioversion, as directed by the tachycardia protocol.

expectedActions.shortAction: Deliver synchronized cardioversion per manufacturer's energy recommendation
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Regular Narrow Complex Tachycardia – Unstable: Deliver a synchronized shock based on manufacturer's recommendations. For responsive patients, consider sedation and analgesia.
expectedActions.rationale: Definitive treatment for unstable SVT unresponsive to reflex compensation.

transitions.condition: Crew proceeds directly to procedural sedation followed by synchronized cardioversion per the unstable pathway, without attempting vagal maneuvers or adenosine.

phases.name: Sedation given, cardioversion performed
phases.description: Crew administers weight-based ketamine for procedural sedation, then delivers a synchronized cardioversion per manufacturer recommendation.
phases.triggerCondition: After confirming the unstable SVT pathway, the crew sedates the responsive patient with ketamine prior to delivering a synchronized shock, per protocol's direction to consider sedation and analgesia for responsive patients undergoing cardioversion.

clinicalPresentation.circulation: Radial pulse rapid, weak, regular; skin pale, cool, diaphoretic
otherFindings: Sedated with ketamine, responds to voice
Pads placed, synchronized mode confirmed on defibrillator

expectedActions.shortAction: Reassess vitals and rhythm; obtain post-conversion 12-lead EKG
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Initial rhythm and all rhythm changes ... Obtain monitor strips after each intervention
expectedActions.rationale: Confirms successful conversion and documents rhythm change for handoff.

transitions.condition: Synchronized cardioversion successfully converts the rhythm to sinus, with rapid improvement in blood pressure and mental status.

phases.name: Converted to sinus rhythm
phases.description: Rhythm converts to sinus following synchronized cardioversion; blood pressure and mental status improve. Crew reassesses vitals, obtains a post-conversion 12-lead, and prepares for transport.
phases.triggerCondition: Following synchronized cardioversion, the patient converts to sinus rhythm with resolution of hypotension and near-syncope.

clinicalPresentation.circulation: Strong, regular radial pulses; skin warm and dry
clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: "That's so much better, my heart feels normal now."

phases.name: Vagal/adenosine attempted despite instability
phases.description: Crew treats the tachycardia as though stable, attempting vagal maneuvers and adenosine despite the patient's hypotension and near-syncope. Time is lost while the patient's perfusion continues to decline.
phases.triggerCondition: Crew follows the stable pharmacologic pathway (vagal maneuvers, adenosine) despite the patient's hypotension and near-syncope meeting unstable criteria, delaying definitive synchronized cardioversion.

clinicalPresentation.circulation: Weak, thready radial pulses; skin pale, cool, diaphoretic
clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: "I feel really dizzy... everything's getting dark..."

expectedActions.shortAction: Abandon the stable pathway; sedate and perform synchronized cardioversion immediately
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Regular Narrow Complex Tachycardia – Unstable: Deliver a synchronized shock based on manufacturer's recommendations. For responsive patients, consider sedation and analgesia.
expectedActions.rationale: Continued deterioration confirms the unstable pathway was indicated from the outset; cardioversion should not be delayed further.
